previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for cycle 25 of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He tolerated the infusion well but experienced delayed clearance of methotrexate, requiring extended hospitalization and increased IV fluids to 200 cc/hr. Leucovorin rescue was continued every six hours, and he was discharged with a three-day course of oral leucovorin. A severe headache prompted a head CT, which showed no acute abnormalities; the headache resolved with acetaminophen. Hypokalemia developed and was managed with supplementation. Rituximab was postponed due to allergy concerns and will be scheduled for the following weekend. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to restart omeprazole and aspirin, continue GenTeal eye drops, and follow up with his oncologist and ophthalmologist.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:
Chest:  Frontal and lateral views

INDICATION:  History: ___ with fatigue/lethargy  // Eval for pna

TECHNIQUE:  Chest Frontal and Lateral

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

The lungs are clear without focal consolidation.  No pleural effusion or
pneumothorax is seen. The aorta is tortuous. The cardiac silhouette is not
enlarged.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute cardiopulmonary process.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with CNS lymphoma, here w/ 1 week of extreme
fatigue/dizziness  // Eval for intracranial hemorrhage/mass effect

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained from the skull base
through the vertex, without IV administration of contrast. Reformatted coronal
and sagittal and thin-section bone algorithm-reconstructed images were
acquired, and all images are viewed in brain and bone window on the
workstation.

DOSE:  DLP (mGy-cm): 891.9.

CTDIvol (mGy): 55.7

COMPARISON:  The study is compared with head CT dated ___, as well
as MRI of the head from ___.

FINDINGS: 

A subtle area of hypodensity in the left thalamus (02:13), extending into the
left cerebral peduncle (02:12) is new compared to the prior CT from ___, and no correlating abnormality in this area was identified on the prior
MRI from ___. There is no intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect,
or acute vascular territorial infarction.  A focal hypodensity in the deep
white matter of the left frontal lobe (02:22) is similar compared to the prior
CT and MRI. The ventricles and sulci are unchanged in size and configuration,
with persistent slight asymmetric enlargement of the left lateral ventricle
compared to the right. There is no shift of the normally midline
structures.The basal cisterns appear patent and there is preservation of the
gray-white matter differentiation.

A left frontal burr hole defect is again seen. No fracture or suspicious
osseous lesion is identified.The included paranasal sinuses, and middle ear
cavities are clear.  The mastoids are underpneumatized.

IMPRESSION:



1. New subtle areas of hypodensity in the left thalamus extending into the
left cerebral peduncle could represent progression of lymphoma. A dedicated
MRI with and without contrast is recommended.
2. No acute intracranial hemorrhage is seen.

EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W AND W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with h/o CNS lymphoma and abnormality on CT scan
___ needs eval for progression of disease  // please eval for progression of
CNS lymphoma. Please do study AM of ___ (after 7AM ok, thanks)

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1, axial T1 pre and postcontrast, axial gradient echo,
FLAIR, T2, diffusion weighted, sagittal MPRAGE postcontrast with coronal and
axial reformats following administration of 7 cc Gadavist.

COMPARISON:  CT brain without contrast ___, MRI head with and without
contrast of ___ and ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is T2/FLAIR hyperintense area, new since the prior MRI of ___
with corresponding slow diffusion centered in the left thalamus extending to
the posterior limb of the internal capsule superiorly and through the left
cerebral peduncle to the left side of pons inferiorly, demonstrating
postcontrast enhancement.
An additional small enhancing gyriform focus of the right posterior occipital
lobe (series 10, image 12) with associated slow diffusion and FLAIR
hyperintensity is noted.
New since prior exam are confluent subcortical and periventricular white
matter FLAIR T2 hyperintense foci distributed in centrum semiovale, corona
radiata, subcortical white matter in the frontal, parietal and occipital lobes
some of which demonstrate slow diffusion (e.g. Posterior right frontal lesion
(series 7, image 17) and bilateral parietal occipital white matter without
associated enhancement.  Diffuse FLAIR hyperintensity involving the splenium
of the corpus callosum is also noted with minimal marginal discontinous
enhancement.
(Se 10, im 13)

Superimposed FLAIR hyperintensities at the left frontal vertex and left
lateral ventricular white matter appear less prominent/unchanged when compared
to prior exams.
There is a single punctate focus of gradient echo susceptibility at the left
frontal vertex, unchanged from prior exam, presumably sequela of prior micro
hemorrhage.

The major flow voids are preserved. Sulci, ventricles and cisterns are within
expected limits.  The visualized paranasal sinuses are essentially clear,
noting asymmetrically small left maxillary sinus. The orbits are unremarkable.
The mastoid air cells are poorly pneumatized essentially clear.


IMPRESSION: 

T2/FLAIR hyperintense area demonstrating postcontrast T1 enhancement and slow
diffusion involving the posterior limb of the internal capsule, left thalamus
and extending into the left cerebral peduncle and left side of the pons.-
A smaller focus of enhancing T2 FLAIR hyperintensity of the right occipital
lobe is also noted.

Superimposed symmetric and confluent bilateral subcortical and periventricular
white matter FLAIR hyperintense foci, some of which demonstrate slow diffusion
without enhancement; diffuse FLAIR hyperintensity of the splenium of the
corpus callosum with minimal marginal enhancement is noted.

Exact etiology uncertain from imaging.  DDx includes progression of the
underlying CNS lmphoma, drug toxicity, demyelinating changes,
inflammatory/autoimmune etiologies, less likely vasculitis/ischemic changes.

Correlate clinically and with labs and close followup to assess for interval
change .

NOTIFICATION:  The findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr.
___ on the telephone on ___ at 4:14 ___, 10 minutes after
discovery of the findings.

EXAMINATION:COMPARISON:  CT ABDOMEN & PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST PART OF CT TORSO

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with hx CNS lymphoma and new brain lesions  //
eval for lymphoma recurrence

TECHNIQUE:  Multi-detector CT of the chest abdomen and pelvis was done with IV
contrast. Split bolus technique. Multiplanar image displays submitted to PACS.
Chest scan will be provided by the chest service

DOSE:  Torso  DLP: 519 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  ___.


FINDINGS:



LOWER CHEST:

Please refer to separate report of CT chest performed on the same day for
description of the thoracic findings.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY:  The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits,
without stones or gallbladder wall thickening.
PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.
SPLEEN:  The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.
ADRENALS:  The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.
URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of stones, focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  A
multilocular cystic lesion is seen in the upper pole of the right kidney,
stable. It contains a fleck of calcification at its center and three locules
are seen as previously.  It measures 7.6 x 5.9 cm
There are no urothelial lesions in the kidneys or ureters. There is no
perinephric abnormality.
GASTROINTESTINAL:  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness and enhancement throughout.  Colon and rectum are within normal
limits. Appendix contains air, has normal caliber without evidence of fat
stranding.  The previously seen focal sigmoid wall thickening is not
appreciated.
RETROPERITONEUM:  There is no evidence of retroperitoneal and mesenteric
lymphadenopathy.
VASCULAR:  There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is no calcium burden
in the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

PELVIS:

The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no evidence
of pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.
REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: Prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

There is no evidence of worrisome lesions. Abdominal and pelvic wall is within
normal limits.


IMPRESSION: 

Essentially normal CT of the abdomen pelvis with no signs of lymphoma. Stable
multilocular cystic lesion in the right kidney

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with CNS lymphoma,
assessment for disease recurrence.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT of the chest was obtained from thoracic inlet to upper
abdomen after administration of IV contrast.  Axial images were reviewed in
conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.

FINDINGS:

Evaluation of the mediastinum reveals no pathologically enlarged mediastinal,
hilar or axillary lymph nodes.  Subcarinal calcified lymph nodes are
unchanged.  The aorta and pulmonary arteries are normal in diameter.  Heart
size is normal.  There is no pericardial or pleural effusion.  The imaged
portion of the upper abdomen will be reviewed separately and the corresponding
report will be issued.

Airways are patent to the subsegmental level bilaterally.

There are no lytic or sclerotic lesions worrisome for infection or neoplasm.

Basal atelectasis and bronchiectasis are unchanged as well as several
subpleural pulmonary nodules.  No masses or consolidations demonstrated.

IMPRESSION:

Stable appearance of the chest.  There is no evidence of intrathoracic
lymphoma recurrence.
